title: Does handing gemma-4-31B the correct entities (oracle perception) flip its GOAL hypothesis to the true win condition? 3-condition ablation over 8 games.
methodology_note: Same model + same learned RULES per game (held constant); only the PERCEPTION varies (A naive HUD/decoy, B +true entities, C +entities+HUD-labeled). Perception facts contain entity presence/role ONLY, never the goal. Source facts read for offline dev analysis (authorized), never used in the hidden submission. Judging of goal-match is done offline by the outer loop.

conditions.A_naive: only the HUD/decoy the segmentation actually surfaced
conditions.B_entities: naive view + true entities (HUD not labeled)
conditions.C_oracle: true entities + HUD explicitly identified as a non-goal counter

per_game.true_win: navigate the player avatar onto the exit tile

A_naive: Change the 3x3 value grid to all 14s.
Change all values in the 3x3 grid to 14.
B_entities: Reach the EXIT tile after toggling the value block near (54,29) to 14.
Reach the EXIT tile while the meter at columns 62-63 is filled.
C_oracle: Reach the EXIT tile after changing the values in the block near (54,29) to a specific required state.
Reach the EXIT tile after changing the values in the block near (54,29) to a specific required state.

judgment.note: C names 'reach the EXIT tile' (+ a spurious value precondition); B cleaner ('Reach the EXIT tile')

per_game.true_win: navigate the player token onto the exit block

B_entities: Move the PLAYER token to the EXIT block.
Move the PLAYER token to the EXIT block.
C_oracle: Move the PLAYER token to the EXIT block.
Move the PLAYER token to the EXIT block.

judgment.note: C exact: 'Move the PLAYER token to the EXIT block'; A was the LOSE condition

per_game.true_win: morph the avatar's shape/color/rotation to match a goal pad, then stand on it

A_naive: Change all floor cells from color 3/5 to color 12.
Recolor all floor cells from 3/5 to 12.
B_entities: Reach a GOAL-PAD tile with the PLAYER avatar.
Reach a GOAL-PAD tile with the PLAYER avatar.
C_oracle: Move the PLAYER avatar to a GOAL-PAD while matching its required shape, color, and rotation.
Move the player avatar to a goal-pad while matching its required shape, color, and rotation.

per_game.true_win: move/rotate pieces so their terminal markers pair up (spatial endpoint pairing)

A_naive: Clear all cells of colors 4, 12, and 14 from the board.
Clear all cells of colors 4, 12, and 14 from the board.
B_entities: Align the terminal marker cells (8 and 13) to specific trigger coordinates to clear the rest of the board.
Align the terminal markers (8 and 13) to specific trigger coordinates to clear the board.
C_oracle: Align the terminal MARKER cells (8 and 13) so they are adjacent or overlapping.
Align the terminal MARKER cells (colors 8 and 13) to specific target coordinates or to each other.

judgment.note: C 'align the terminal markers 8/13' = the endpoint-pairing win

per_game.true_win: merge blocks until only one (goal count) remains

A_naive: Change all cells in row 0 to state 1.
Fill all cells in row 0 with the state 1.
B_entities: Clear all blocks from the board.
Clear all blocks from the board.
C_oracle: Clear all blocks from the board.
Clear all blocks from the board.

judgment.note: right objects+merge frame ('clear all blocks') but wrong count target (reduce-to-ONE, not clear-all)

per_game.true_win: maneuver the player sprite (via gravity) onto the gem tile

A_naive: Fill row 63 entirely with color-15 cells.
Fill row 63 entirely with color-15 cells.
B_entities: Fill row 63 entirely with color-15 cells.
Fill row 63 entirely with color-15 cells.

judgment.note: ONLY C flipped ('reach the GEM'); B stayed HUD-fixated -> HUD-labeling (suppression) was necessary, not just adding entities

per_game.true_win: slide each piece onto its matching target pad

A_naive: Set all cells from (21,0) to (42,0) to 5.
Set all cells in the range (21,0) through (42,0) to 5.
B_entities: Move all PIECE objects onto their matching TARGET-PAD tiles.
Move all PIECE objects onto their matching TARGET-PAD tiles.
C_oracle: Move all PIECE objects onto their matching TARGET-PAD tiles.
Move all PIECE objects onto their matching TARGET-PAD tiles.

judgment.note: exact ('move each PIECE onto its matching TARGET-PAD'); dynamics contrast case flipped on perception alone

per_game.true_win: satisfy the hidden adjacency-color pattern constraint over the tiles

A_naive: Reach a specific target cell on the grid.
Reach a specific target cell on the grid.
B_entities: Arrange the colored blocks into a specific hidden pattern by clicking them.
Arrange the colored blocks into a specific hidden pattern.
C_oracle: Arrange the colored blocks into a specific hidden adjacency-color pattern.
Arrange the blocks to match a specific hidden color adjacency pattern.

judgment.note: C 'match the hidden adjacency-color pattern' = the true CSP win; deepest contrast case still flipped

headline: DECISIVE POSITIVE: under NAIVE perception 0/8 goals correct (replicating the 8/8-never-hypothesized diagnosis); under ORACLE perception (correct entities + HUD labeled) 7/8 correct + 1/8 partial (lf52). The goal-hypothesis generator is NOT the bottleneck -- it produces the TRUE win condition as soon as perception delivers the right entities. bp35 shows BOTH halves matter: adding entities (B) did NOT flip it; only labeling the row-63 bar as a lose-timer (C) did. Confirms GAP-ARC-PERCEPTION-HUD-VS-BOARD as THE lever and justifies building the HUD-register + mover/entity detectors.
honest_caveats: This measures GOAL-HYPOTHESIS correctness, NOT level discovery. Right goal is necessary, not sufficient: the agent must still EXECUTE it (navigate/merge/two-click), which needs the dynamics/action model (bp35 gravity, r11l two-click remain execution gaps even with the right goal).
Oracle facts were hand-authored from source (offline dev). A real detector must PRODUCE these from frames autonomously -- that is the build this ablation justifies, not a shipped capability.
Single temperature (0.3), 2 seeds; goals were highly stable across seeds. Small n (8 games).
